questions.prompt: A reply holds read a.ts, read b.ts, edit a.ts, read a.ts. When does the last read start?
options: At the same time as the first two reads
After the edit finishes, because the edit is a barrier
Before the edit, because reads go first
questions.explanation: The edit is not concurrency-safe, so it runs alone and nothing after it starts until it is done. The last read therefore sees the edited file.

questions.prompt: A tool's isConcurrencySafe returns undefined because the author forgot a return statement. How is the call run?
options: Alone, as a barrier, because only exactly true counts as safe
In parallel, because undefined is not false
It is rejected with an error
In parallel, but only with other tools of the same name
questions.explanation: The check is === true. Anything else is treated as unsafe, which costs some time but never risks a clash.

questions.prompt: In a group, read b.ts finishes before read a.ts. In what order are the results returned?
options: b.ts first, because it finished first
In the order the model asked: a.ts then b.ts
Whichever order the event log stored them
questions.explanation: Each result is written into its own slot by index, so the returned list matches the model's order regardless of finishing order.
